set.body:
From the re-review of c566de3ca (S3d-2 graph reader). None reaches the real part-b graph (all names ASCII, one part), but each is a fail-open or untested path:
1. Unicode version: Python (Unicode 16.0) and the JDK lowercase 27 code points differently, so the reader can match names the core would not. Pin the version or refuse names with code points outside the shared version.
2. The graph's part is the caller's word: load(..., part=) is not checked against anything in the graph. Derive it from the edition id or have the writer emit the part.
3. _TIME uses \d, which matches non-ASCII digits; use [0-9] or re.ASCII.
4. Malformed record arguments (words=None, a non-dict word, span with None, span_text=None) raise untyped errors instead of RecordRefusal.
5. Load-bearing conditions with no killing test (single-condition mutants survive): _increasing on mention intervals (a reversed interval would overlap any record spanning it); the Java trim character set (Python strip() would let a trailing non-ASCII space bind); the lower and upper edition-extent bounds; 0 <= word start; the _TIME fraction form ("10." accepted by a mutant). The reviewer's driver is scratchpad mut3.py (session-local).
set.title: S3d-2 follow-ups: Unicode version, graph part, ASCII digits, typed record refusals, courts
